edges.description: Loss of PGM2L1 phosphoglucomutase activity reduces glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and other sugar bisphosphate concentrations in patient fibroblasts.
Reduced brain glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and sugar bisphosphate concentrations in PGM2L1 deficiency are associated with severe global developmental delay through an as-yet unknown brain-metabolic role.
Reduced brain glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and sugar bisphosphate concentrations in PGM2L1 deficiency are associated with severe speech and language delay through an as-yet unknown brain-metabolic role.
Reduced brain glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and sugar bisphosphate concentrations in PGM2L1 deficiency are associated with seizures through an as-yet unknown brain-metabolic role.

nodes.description: Severe developmental delay was present in all four originally reported individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: All four had severe developmental and speech delay, dysmorphic facial features, ear anomalies, high arched palate, strabismus, hypotonia, and keratosis pilaris.

meta.association: Bi-allelic inactivating variants in PGM2L1 cause this neurodevelopmental disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Four individuals (three females and one male aged between 2 and 7.5 years) with bi-allelic inactivating mutations of PGM2L1 were identified by exome sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: Delineating the Adult Phenotype of PGM2L1 -Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
evidence.snippet: In 2021, biallelic pathogenic variants in the PGM2L1 gene were first linked to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized primarily by developmental delay in four pediatric cases.

nodes.description: Bi-allelic inactivating PGM2L1 variants abolish or severely reduce the glucose-1,6-bisphosphate synthase activity of PGM2L1, a brain-enriched paralog of phosphoglucomutase 2.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: We describe a genetic syndrome due to PGM2L1 deficiency. PGM2 and PGM2L1 make hexose-bisphosphates, like glucose-1,6-bisphosphate, which are indispensable cofactors for sugar phosphomutases.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: While PGM2 has a wide tissue distribution, PGM2L1 is highly expressed in the brain, accounting for the elevated concentrations of glucose-1,6-bisphosphate found there.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts show markedly reduced glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and other sugar bisphosphates, though residual concentrations remain sufficient to maximally stimulate phosphomutases, so protein glycosylation (LAMP2 glycosylation, serum transferrin glycosylation) is unaffected. This distinguishes PGM2L1 deficiency mechanistically from the congenital disorders of glycosylation.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the children's fibroblasts showed that glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and other sugar bisphosphates were markedly reduced but still present at concentrations able to stimulate phosphomutases maximally.

evidence.reference_title: Impaired glucose-1,6-biphosphate production due to bi-allelic PGM2L1 mutations is associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Hence, the concentrations of NDP-sugars and glycosylation of the heavily glycosylated protein LAMP2 were normal. Consistent with this, serum transferrin was normally glycosylated in affected individuals. PGM2L1 deficiency does not appear to be a glycosylation defect
